source.note: 英文逐字稿取自 YouTube 字幕；中文為學習用翻譯。版權屬原作者，僅供個人學習。

lines.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Neil.
lines.zh: 哈囉，這裡是 BBC Learning English 的《6 Minute English》。我是 Neil。

lines.en: And I'm Pippa.
lines.zh: 我是 Pippa。

lines.en: In this episode we're discussing poetry.
lines.zh: 這一集我們要討論詩。

lines.en: For some, poetry is what you study at school, then forget, while for others it becomes an important part of their life.
lines.zh: 對有些人來說，詩是在學校念一念、之後就忘了的東西；對另一些人來說，詩卻成了生活中很重要的一部分。

lines.en: Have you ever read or written any poetry, Neil?
lines.zh: Neil，你讀過或寫過詩嗎？

lines.en: Well, I haven't written any poetry since I was at school.
lines.zh: 嗯，我離開學校後就沒寫過詩了。

lines.en: I would love to read more poetry, but I just don't get it, really.
lines.zh: 我很想多讀一點詩，但我就是看不懂。

lines.en: I find it difficult to understand.
lines.zh: 我覺得詩很難理解。

lines.en: A good place to hear poetry is an open mic night, a live event where anyone is allowed to stand up on stage to sing or recite poems.
lines.zh: 聽詩的好地方是開放麥克風之夜，這是一種任何人都可以上台唱歌或朗誦詩的現場活動。

lines.en: Here, BBC reporter Maria recites her open mic poem about a friend who suffered a stroke, for BBC World Service programme People Fixing the World.
lines.zh: 在這裡，BBC 記者 Maria 為 BBC 世界廣播節目《People Fixing the World》朗誦她在開放麥克風之夜念的詩，內容是關於一位中風的朋友。

lines.en: This first poem, I wrote it about a friend who I love dearly.
lines.zh: 這第一首詩，是我寫給一位我非常愛的朋友。

lines.en: It's called Stroke.
lines.zh: 它叫〈中風〉。

lines.en: You're awake And trying to grasp who it is.
lines.zh: 你醒著，努力想認出來的是誰。

lines.en: I pull my mask past my lips and you study my face, Eyes wide.
lines.zh: 我把口罩拉下嘴唇，你端詳我的臉，睜大雙眼。

lines.en: I've enough stuff to tell you, I say, Sinking into a chair.
lines.zh: 「我有好多事要告訴你」，我說，一邊陷進椅子裡。

lines.en: I stare.
lines.zh: 我凝視著。

lines.en: Sometimes if you go to an open mic night, people can really touch your soul with what they're saying.
lines.zh: 有時候去開放麥克風之夜，別人說的話真的能觸動你的靈魂。

lines.en: And even if you're having a bad day, life can feel so much better after going to an open mic night.
lines.zh: 就算你那天過得很糟，去過開放麥克風之夜後，生活也會感覺好很多。

lines.en: For Maria, poetry has the power to heal emotions and touch your soul, meaning to affect you deeply on an emotional or spiritual level.
lines.zh: 對 Maria 來說，詩有療癒情緒、觸動靈魂的力量，也就是在情感或心靈層面深深影響你。

lines.en: In this episode, we'll hear more about the positive power of poetry and, as usual, we'll learn some useful new words and phrases.
lines.zh: 在這一集，我們會聽到更多關於詩的正面力量，一如往常也會學一些實用的新單字和片語。

lines.en: And remember, you'll find all the vocabulary, plus a quiz and worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
lines.zh: 別忘了，所有詞彙以及測驗和學習單都在我們的網站 bbclearningenglish.com。

lines.en: But first, I have a question for you, Pippa.
lines.zh: 不過首先，Pippa，我有個問題要問你。

lines.en: Just now you used the phrase 'the positive power of poetry', repeating the same initial 'p' sound across a string of words.
lines.zh: 你剛剛用了「the positive power of poetry」這個說法，在一串字裡重複同一個開頭的 p 音。

lines.en: Doing this is a common feature of poetry, but what's it called?
lines.zh: 這是詩很常見的特色，但這叫什麼？

lines.en: Is it: a) assonance, b) alliteration, or c) simile?
lines.zh: 是：a) 諧母音（assonance）、b) 頭韻（alliteration），還是 c) 明喻（simile）？

lines.en: Hmm. Finally, my English degree might come in handy!
lines.zh: 嗯。我的英文學位終於要派上用場了！

lines.en: And I'm going to say b) alliteration.
lines.zh: 我要選 b) 頭韻（alliteration）。

lines.en: Well, we'll find out at the end, and I hope you don't get embarrassed, Pippa!
lines.zh: 我們會在最後揭曉，希望你不會尷尬喔，Pippa！

lines.en: Now, poetry helped Maria overcome sadness, but could its power to heal work in other areas too?
lines.zh: 詩幫助 Maria 走出了悲傷，但它的療癒力量在其他領域也有用嗎？

lines.en: Hot Poets is a group helping people understand the science behind global issues like climate change.
lines.zh: Hot Poets 是一個幫助大家理解氣候變遷等全球議題背後科學的團體。

lines.en: They go to meetings like the UN Climate Conference and listen to scientific papers being presented.
lines.zh: 他們會去參加聯合國氣候大會之類的會議，聽別人發表科學論文。

lines.en: Then they write a poem about it all and perform that back to the audience.
lines.zh: 然後他們把這些內容寫成詩，再表演給聽眾聽。

lines.en: Here's Hot Poet Liv Torc, reciting her poem to BBC World Service's People Fixing the World.
lines.zh: 這是 Hot Poets 的成員 Liv Torc 為 BBC 世界廣播《People Fixing the World》朗誦她的詩。

lines.en: It starts with an adventure at sea, A big blue murder mystery, where the killer is not the whale But an epic humanity fail Of overfishing and polluting at unimaginable scale.
lines.zh: 故事從一場海上冒險開始，一部湛藍的謀殺懸疑劇，兇手不是鯨魚，而是人類的一場史詩級失敗——規模大到難以想像的過度捕撈和污染。

lines.en: Liv's poem is based on a study into biodiversity.
lines.zh: Liv 的詩是根據一項生物多樣性研究寫成的。

lines.en: It's a complex research project that many find hard to understand.
lines.zh: 那是一個很多人都難以理解的複雜研究計畫。

lines.en: Here, Liv discusses this with Myra Anubi for BBC World Service programme People Fixing the World: And Liv, I mean, so what you've identified is that there is an issue around the communication of science.
lines.zh: 在這裡，Liv 在 BBC 世界廣播節目《People Fixing the World》中和 Myra Anubi 討論這件事：Liv，所以你發現的是，科學的溝通方式有問題。

lines.en: Yes, a lot of this jargon is really hard to understand, or a lot of the science is quite impenetrable to normal people, so it's instantly a turn-off.
lines.zh: 對，很多術語真的很難懂，或者很多科學內容對一般人來說相當艱澀難懂，所以一下子就讓人失去興趣。

lines.en: Science uses lots of jargon – specialist or technical vocabulary which is quite different from everyday language.
lines.zh: 科學用了很多 jargon（術語）——和日常用語很不一樣的專業或技術詞彙。

lines.en: For example, a scientist might use the word precipitation, while in everyday English we would say rain.
lines.zh: 例如，科學家可能會用 precipitation（降水）這個字，而日常英文我們會說 rain（雨）。

lines.en: Jargon can make scientific papers impenetrable, an adjective meaning impossible to understand.
lines.zh: 術語會讓科學論文 impenetrable，這個形容詞的意思是完全無法理解。

lines.en: And worse, it makes science a turn-off – something that people dislike or find uninteresting.
lines.zh: 更糟的是，它讓科學變成 a turn-off——讓人討厭或覺得無趣的東西。

lines.en: Hot Poets try to change all of that by making complex environmental ideas easy to understand through poetry.
lines.zh: Hot Poets 試著透過詩，把複雜的環境概念變得容易理解，來改變這一切。

lines.en: And it works, says Kat Bruce, the environmental scientist whose study Liv based her poem on, talking here with Myra Anubi for BBC World Service's People Fixing the World.
lines.zh: 環境科學家 Kat Bruce 說這確實有效，Liv 的詩就是根據她的研究寫的，她在這裡和 Myra Anubi 在 BBC 世界廣播《People Fixing the World》中對談。

lines.en: What did it mean for you, Kat, hearing the poem, having actually experienced everything she's saying?
lines.zh: Kat，聽到這首詩，而且她說的一切你都親身經歷過，這對你來說有什麼意義？

lines.en: It still gives me goosebumps when I hear it now.
lines.zh: 我現在再聽，還是會起雞皮疙瘩。

lines.en: I think it's everything that I wish I could say and put into words myself.
lines.zh: 我覺得那就是我所有希望自己能說出來、化成文字的東西。

lines.en: I feel like Liv just, you know, has done that.
lines.zh: 我覺得 Liv 就是，你知道，把它做到了。

lines.en: Liv's poem gave Kat goosebumps, meaning she was so emotionally affected that the hairs on her skin stood up, making tiny bumps.
lines.zh: Liv 的詩讓 Kat 起了 goosebumps，意思是她情緒受到很大觸動，皮膚上的汗毛豎起來，形成小小的疙瘩。

lines.en: Maybe poetry can't fix everything, but for Kat, it's making an impact for good.
lines.zh: 也許詩不能解決所有事，但對 Kat 來說，它正在帶來正面的影響。

lines.en: Now, what was the answer to your question, Neil?
lines.zh: 好，Neil，你的問題答案是什麼？

lines.en: Well, you seemed very clear, Pippa, that when you use a string of words beginning with the same sound, it's called alliteration...
lines.zh: 嗯，Pippa，你似乎很確定，一串字用同樣的音開頭，叫做頭韻（alliteration）……

lines.en: and you're absolutely right.
lines.zh: 你完全正確。

lines.en: Phew!
lines.zh: 呼！

lines.en: OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with open mic night, a live event where anyone is allowed to perform poems or music on stage.
lines.zh: 好。我們來複習學到的詞彙，首先是 open mic night，一種任何人都可以上台表演詩或音樂的現場活動。

lines.en: If something touches your soul, it affects you deeply on an emotional or spiritual level.
lines.zh: 如果某件事 touches your soul，就是它在情感或心靈層面深深影響你。

lines.en: Jargon means special words and phrases that are used in a particular profession or subject.
lines.zh: Jargon 是某個行業或學科使用的特殊字詞和說法。

lines.en: The adjective impenetrable means impossible to understand.
lines.zh: 形容詞 impenetrable 的意思是完全無法理解。

lines.en: A turn-off is something that people dislike or find uninteresting.
lines.zh: A turn-off 是讓人討厭或覺得無趣的東西。

lines.en: And finally, if you get goosebumps, the hairs on your skin stand up because you're cold, emotionally affected, or afraid.
lines.zh: 最後，如果你起 goosebumps，就是因為冷、情緒受到觸動或害怕，皮膚上的汗毛豎起來。

lines.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but remember, you'll find lots more episodes as well as a quiz and worksheet for this one on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
lines.zh: 我們的六分鐘又到了，但別忘了，我們的網站 bbclearningenglish.com 上有更多集數，還有這一集的測驗和學習單。

lines.en: See you again soon.
lines.zh: 很快再見。

lines.en: But for now it's goodbye.
lines.zh: 但現在要說再見了。

lines.en: Goodbye!
lines.zh: 再見！
